claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can be used to consolidate powder-based metallic materials.
Machine learning–optimized SPS can reduce the temperature required for full densification without compromising microstructural integrity.
Conventional high-temperature sintering typically requires high energy input and leads to unwanted grain growth.
SPS electric-pulse characteristics, heating rate, dwell time, and applied pressure can be optimized using a data-driven machine-learning model.
A temperature of approximately 900–1000 °C represents the lower end of the relevant SPS process window.
Rapid localized heating and electric-field-assisted diffusion promote densification while suppressing excessive grain growth.
Pulsed electric currents and applied pressure in SPS create localized heating and enhanced diffusion paths.
Localized heating and enhanced diffusion paths permit particle bonding at lower temperatures.
Machine-learning optimization can balance densification and grain-size control.
ML-optimized SPS can achieve full densification at a lower temperature than conventional furnace sintering.
The lower-temperature SPS process can preserve a fine microstructure and mechanical properties.
Conventional furnace sintering typically requires higher temperatures and longer dwell times than SPS.
The higher temperatures and longer dwell times of conventional furnace sintering can cause microstructural coarsening and greater energy consumption.
The effectiveness of SPS temperature reduction depends on powder composition and its response to electric-field-assisted sintering.
The optimal SPS parameter range may be narrow and require separate calibration for different material systems.
The exact temperature reduction and material-specific boundary conditions remain uncertain pending experimental validation.
